doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Duo repertoire and medleys
summary: Cameron describes her ideas for medleys such as Blue Skies with a modulating bridge, and new numbers like Wouldn't It Be Loverly.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Can you talk about your repertoire?
[laughs] Brown, C.: [laughs] I could show you. It‟s over in the bag over there.

[laughs] Brown, C.: No, Sheila has amazing ideas about fitting certain things together and, and working on these medleys. It‟s her million dollar ears, boy. You know, she does, uh, Blue Skies and sings
the bridge up a half step. And then she sang me my line to get us modulated back to the original key in the last A section. [laughs]
Oh. Did I? Okay. [laughs] Brown, C.: Well, Sheila, how do we get back to… [laughs] You know. And um, I contribute stuff from time to time and…
Yeah. Brown, C.: It‟s just, um… it‟s a wide, wide range. I mean, the new stuff in the repertoire lately is, is Wouldn‟t It Be Loverly.
Yeah. Brown, C.: Sheila just had a thing for that. It‟s also… it turns out to be wonderful vehicle for scatting, I think. The changes on it just…
Mm-hmm. Brown, C.: You know… What else have we been doing?
Well, you talked about certain thematic, um, sets you had. Remember, you said something about…
